original_question: Can one define a mathematically robust category of wild virtual knots, formulate its axioms, and prove a theorem describing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence between those links?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual open problem: it already captures the three core demands almost verbatim—define a category of wild virtual knots, formulate its axioms, and prove a theorem explaining when wild equivalence of tame virtual links implies tame equivalence. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The exact target is an open problem in the paper’s problem list, namely Section 7, item 17, titled "Wild Virtuals," rather than a theorem or conjecture proved earlier in the paper. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

To make the question stand alone in the paper’s own framework, it helps to state the ambient model for virtual links used throughout the paper: virtual knot theory is presented as the study of embeddings of curves in thickened surfaces of arbitrary genus, up to addition and removal of empty handles. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The nearby precise topological formulation the paper supplies is the stable-equivalence model: embeddings of links in thickened surfaces S_g × R are considered up to isotopy in the thickened surface, homeomorphisms of the surface, and addition or subtraction of empty handles. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper’s wording distinguishes between the first task, which asks for a category of wild virtual knots, and the second task, which asks for a theorem about tame virtual links; that knots/links distinction should be preserved. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper does not itself define "wild virtual knot," "tame virtual link," or "wild equivalence"; those notions are left implicit and are part of what the open problem asks the reader to formalize. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

No extra hypotheses about orientation, component number, ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, operator conventions, or asymptotic quantifiers appear here; adding such restrictions would go beyond the paper’s statement. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: Within the paper’s topological model of virtual knot theory—where virtual links are represented by stable equivalence classes of embeddings of links in thickened surfaces S_g × R, with stable equivalence generated by isotopy in the thickened surface, homeomorphisms of the surface, and addition or subtraction of empty handles—can one define a category of wild virtual knots, state explicit axioms for that category, and prove a criterion specifying when a wild equivalence between two tame virtual links implies that those links are tamely equivalent as virtual links? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the paper’s theorem that virtual link diagrams are exactly stable equivalence classes of link embeddings in thickened surfaces, can one formulate a surface-theoretic notion of wild stable equivalence for possibly wild link embeddings in S_g × R and determine when wild stable equivalence between tame embeddings forces ordinary stable equivalence of those tame embeddings? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s Problem 17 almost word for word, so the right refinement is to sharpen rather than broaden it. The only substantial paper-based context needed to make it self-contained is the paper’s standard interpretation of virtual links via embeddings in thickened surfaces and the stable-equivalence theorem of Section 2.2; beyond that, the paper intentionally leaves the notions of wildness, tameness, and wild equivalence to be axiomatized as part of the problem itself. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
